Races/Dragonborn.title: Dragonborn
Races/Dragonborn.content:
The Dragonborn of Rathoria are a localized and stable society, distinguished by their geographic concentration and the presence of innate magical abilities.
Geography and Diplomacy

Location: Dragonborn reside on a sovereign island separate from the main continent.
External Relations: Their interaction with other nations is primarily limited to trade. While they do not harbor animosity toward other races or practice strict isolationism, there is a cultural preference to remain on their home island. Consequently, Dragonborn travelers are an uncommon sight in continental Rathoria.

Governance

Council of Elders: The society is governed by a council consisting of the oldest members of the race. Authority is tied directly to age and perceived experience.

Relationship with the Weave

Innate Magic: Unlike most other races in Rathoria who struggle with the Weave or require external divine intervention, some Dragonborn are born with Sorcerous powers.
Uniqueness: They are among the only races that still occasionally possess innate magic.

Races/Dwarves.title: Dwarves
Races/Dwarves.content:
Dwarves are predictable most of them living in Caverns and cities built long before any mortal being remembers practicing traditions held for even longer than that.
Presence and Adaptability

Distribution: Mostly sequestered in the Mountains there are several hubs of dwarves spread throughout the Continent, Large cities will often have several Dwarfish craftsmen, rarely some dwarves have been known to take up work in a very small town preferring the slower pace of life.  These are the most daring and adventurous who desire to see the world even in those cases it tends to not last long in the span of their lives staying 40-50 years before returning to the Mountains.
Societal Structure: The Dwarves of each region recognize a King.

The Weave and Magic
The Dwarves draw mastery from the weave with complex runes and symbols. Any non ancient artifacts and magic items are forged deep within their cities though they very rarely leave.

Mastery: Few Dwarves spend the time to learn Wizardry or Nature magic opting instead for the crafting of weapons, armor and defenses engraved with runes that harness Arcane magic.
Ancient Legends: Among dwarves an ancient prophecies state that they will be the last ones standing firm at the end of the world.

Faith and Divinity
The Dwarves worship the god of Knowledge, Logic and reason. With priests of this god either taking care of the ancient libraries and tomes hidden within the cities or teaching the new craftsmen the intricacies of the runes.

Races/Elves.title: Elves
Races/Elves.content:
The Elves are a sequestered and isolationist race, serving as the primary custodians of arcane knowledge in Rathoria.
Geography and Access


Locations: Elves primarily reside in deep forests, the Feywild, and the sovereign city of Elantria.


The Feywild: Material Plane Elves have maintained semi-consistent access to the Feywild for hundreds of years, a feat unique among the races of Rathoria.


Isolationism: Gaining entry into an Elven city is an arduous process requiring significant persuasion and a high degree of mutual trust. Such integration is rare, leaving the general populace with little knowledge of Elven culture.


Arcane Dominance


The Center of Learning: The city of Elantria is the uncontested center of all magical learning in the realm.


Arcane Power: Elves constitute the vast majority of the continent’s arcane power, possessing a mastery over the Weave that far exceeds other races.


Faith and Worship


The Weave: The primary focus of Elven reverence is the Weave itself, rather than personified deities.


Divine Status: Most Elves are only nominal followers of smaller, random gods. They generally lack the intense, focused devotion to the Mantles seen in human cultures.

Races/Gnomes.title: Gnomes
Races/Gnomes.content:
Gnomes are a ubiquitous and highly assimilated race in Rathoria, found within nearly every society and people group across the continent.
Culture and Society


Assimilation: Gnomes do not possess a unique land or a centralized sovereign culture. Instead, they integrate into the societies of other races. Often serving as the the artisans while Halflings produce the agricultural goods


Communes: While they lack a nation of their own, they frequently establish independent communes located within the borders of other nations.


Universal Presence: They are found among every people group, having successfully integrated into various cultural environments.


Arcane Connection


Wizardry: Gnomes have deep, inherent ties to magic.


Sources of Magic: They are one of the few consistent sources of Wizardry and arcane study outside of the Elven lands. This proficiency distinguishes them from humans, who struggle with the intricacies of spellcasting.


Political and Diplomatic Status


Perceived Threat: Major powers and nations generally do not view Gnomes as a significant military or political threat.


Freedom of Movement: Due to their non-threatening status, Gnomes are often granted a form of informal immunity, allowing them to travel across borders and through different nations as they please. This mobility remains largely unaffected by the political tensions or trade blockades currently restricting other races.

Races/Goliaths.title: Goliaths
Races/Goliaths.content:
Goliaths are a nomadic and physically formidable race inhabiting the highest reaches of the continent.
Geography and Habitat


Location: Goliaths roam the mountain ranges situated above the ancient fortresses of the Dwarves.


Environment: They occupy high-altitude, rugged terrain that remains inaccessible to most other races.


Physical Attributes


Durability: Goliaths are known for being incredibly durable, capable of surviving the harsh conditions of the peaks.


Prowess: Their physical prowess is unmatched by many of the other races in Rathoria.


Society and Knowledge


Social Structure: They live in roaming colonies rather than permanent settlements.


External Relations: Little is known about their way of life or their diplomatic relations with other nations. They remain an enigmatic presence on the continent, largely disconnected from the political scrambling of the Kingdoms and Republics below.

Races/Half-Elves.title: Half-Elves
Races/Half-Elves.content:
Despite the extreme difficulty of integrating into Elven society, Half-elves are more prevalent across Rathoria than demographic expectations would suggest.
Lineage and History


Multigenerational Heritage: A significant majority of Half-elves are born to parents who are both Half-elves themselves.


Ancient Mingling: The current prevalence of “true-breeding” Half-elf lineages suggests a historical era when Humans and Elves mingled much more commonly than they do in the present age.

Races/Halflings.title: Halflings
Races/Halflings.content:
Halflings in Rathoria are defined by their connection to the land, split between pastoral agriculturalists and deep-woodland guardians.
Subgroups and Lifestyles
The Homesteaders (Agricultural)


Lifestyle: Similar to Gnomes, these halflings focus on agrarian life, taking care of farms and cultivating the land.


Societal Structure: They typically group together in small, tight-knit villages. Often with gnomes, they often exist within or alongside the borders of larger nations, maintaining a peaceful, communal existence.


Role: They are known as primary producers of food and resources within the societies they inhabit.


The Woodland Halflings (Druidic)


Habitat: These halflings inhabit the deep woodlands that the Elves do not occupy. They live in the untamed parts of the world.


Nature Attunement: They are deeply in tune with the natural world and the raw forces of nature.


Societal Structure:


Druidic Circles: Many are organized into powerful druidic circles that manage and protect their forest domains.


Dwelling: They are often nomadic, following the cycles of the forest, or live in small villages constructed entirely from local natural resources.

Races/Humans.title: Humans
Races/Humans.content:
Humans are the most diverse race in Rathoria, both in culture and location. Unlike most races, they defy easy generalizations regarding government, philosophy, or social behavior.
Presence and Adaptability

Distribution: Humans are found across the entire world. A common saying suggests that anywhere a rat or a cockroach can survive, a human is likely to be found.
Societal Structure: Humans do not adhere to a single governing style; they are equally represented within Kingdoms, Theocracies, City-states, and Republics.

The Weave and Magic
The intricacies of the Weave generally escape the human race.

Mastery: Very few humans are capable of the complex nuances required for arcane spellcasting.
The Lifespan Theory: The prevailing academic thought is that the human lifespan is simply too short to allow for the mastery of the art within a single lifetime.
Ancient Legends: Old wives’ tales persist regarding ancient circles of powerful human Magi who once possessed magical capabilities that rivaled those of the Elves and the Dwarves.

Faith and Divinity
Worship of the gods is strongest among the human population.

Service and Miracles: Through devoted service, humans are frequently granted miracles by the gods.
Divine Alignment: Human countries and cities often align themselves with a specific deity, seeking protection and blessings in exchange for their collective faith and devotion.

Races/Planar-Touched.title: Planar Touched
Races/Planar-Touched.content:
Tieflings and Aasimar represent the rare physical manifestations of planar influence in Rathoria. Unlike other races, they do not have established civilizations or a shared history; they are individual anomalies.
Rarity and Origin

Scarcity: Both races are exceedingly rare. Their existence is tied to direct communication with Fiends (for Tieflings) or Gods (for Aasimar).
Infrequent Contact: Because direct communication with planar entities is an outlier event, the resulting “blessings” or “curses” that create these bloodlines are equally uncommon.

Societal Perception

Stigma and Legend: Stories of these individuals possessing unholy power or being born warlocks are common.
Pacts: While the general populace often assumes these individuals have made dangerous pacts, most do not actually possess such formal agreements. Their power is often innate rather than negotiated.

Lifestyle and Distribution

Integration: There are no Tiefling or Aasimar enclaves. Depending on the tolerance of their home region, they either remain where they were born or are forced into a nomadic lifestyle.
Nomadism: Many become wanderers, either by choice or due to the suspicion their appearance and heritage arouse in sequestered communities.
